headline: January's company-wide 28.7% revenue drop is the normal December-to-January seasonal reset, not a business event.

evidence.what: Jan-2025 net revenue vs the December peak (MoM) vs Jan-2024 (YoY)
evidence.figures: Dec-2024 EUR 15,965,841 -> Jan-2025 EUR 11,383,322 (-28.7% MoM); Jan-2024 EUR 11,098,719 -> Jan-2025 +2.6% YoY, positive at every BU (Baltics +5.2%)

evidence.what: December seasonal build is the same both years
evidence.figures: Nov->Dec build +12.6% (2024) and +11.0% (2025); December is the annual peak, January the trough in both years

recommended_action: No action; the deterministic MoM flag is measuring the calendar and can be read against YoY instead.

headline: The continuous Nordics material-cost flags are pure volume growth, not input-cost inflation; unit material cost is flat and below budget.

evidence.what: Nordics material cost per unit, FY2024 vs FY2025
evidence.figures: 1.31 -> 1.30 EUR/unit (-1.5%); total material cost +11.5% is driven by volume +13.2% (23.3m units)

evidence.what: Nordics 2025 actual vs budget on volume and unit material cost
evidence.figures: volume +10.6% vs budget; actual material 1.2952 vs budget 1.3052 EUR/unit (favourable); the vs-budget breach is more units at a lower unit cost

recommended_action: Stand down on procurement; redirect attention to realised price/discount, which is where the Nordics margin is actually leaking (see F4, F7).

headline: Baltics revenue really is up ~27%, but it is bought volume: discounts rose to 12.5% and EBITDA fell 8.1% YoY, so the revenue beat is value-destructive.
claimed_cause: Baltics grew volume +32.9% by lifting the promo discount rate from 8.0% to 12.5% (rising every month, 8.2% in Jan to 17.1% in Dec) and out-spending budget on S&M and admin; realised net price fell 4.4% and gross margin fell 2.9pp, so EBITDA came in below both prior year and budget.

evidence.what: Baltics volume, net price/unit, discount rate and gross margin FY2024 vs FY2025
evidence.figures: volume +32.9%; net revenue +27.1%; net/unit -4.4%; discount 8.0%->12.5% (Jan 8.2% climbing to Dec 17.1%); gross margin 41.4%->38.5%

evidence.what: Baltics EBITDA YoY and the vs-budget decomposition
evidence.figures: EBITDA EUR 3,209,582 -> 2,949,511 (-8.1% YoY); FY2025 vs budget -816,928 = gross profit +1,440,283 undone by S&M -1,329,976 and admin -927,234

recommended_action: Put Baltics discount and S&M policy on the agenda: cap the discount ladder and require incremental volume to clear a contribution-margin hurdle.

headline: The EBITDA-vs-budget miss (-EUR 3.4m reported, -EUR 5.6m ex one-off) is real and is a margin problem in Nordics plus unprofitable growth in Baltics; Central Europe is not the cause.
claimed_cause: Company reported EBITDA is EUR 3.44m below budget (EUR 5.64m below excluding the EUR 2.2m April one-off). Nordics is the bulk: gross profit EUR 4.23m under budget from Home Care discounting, not opex. Baltics adds a EUR 0.82m miss where above-budget gross profit is more than consumed by S&M and admin overspend. Central Europe's -EUR 0.44m is minor.

evidence.what: FY2025 EBITDA vs budget by BU, decomposed
evidence.figures: Nordics -2,179,152 (of which gross profit -4,230,925, +2,200,000 other income masking); Baltics -816,928 (gross profit +1,440,283, S&M -1,329,976, admin -927,234); Central Europe -440,506; Company -3,436,586

evidence.what: EBITDA YoY, reported vs underlying (ex other income)
evidence.figures: Company reported -1.4% but underlying -13.7% (17,956,325 -> 15,497,896); Nordics underlying -28.5% (masked to -6.1%); Central Europe +12.4%

recommended_action: Board agenda item: the EBITDA miss is a Nordics/Baltics pricing-and-discount problem; hold the review there and treat the reported figure as flattered by EUR 2.2m.

headline: Central Europe's DSO deterioration to ~77 days is almost entirely one account, Rheinkauf Gruppe, whose receivable tripled and who now pays at 116 days against 45-day terms.
claimed_cause: Central Europe closing receivables rose EUR 2.81m over 2025 while collections stayed flat; Rheinkauf Gruppe alone accounts for EUR 2.43m (87%) of that build, its implied DSO moving from 55.6 to 116.2 days against 45-day contractual terms. Two Benelux distributors stretched more mildly; all other CE accounts sit near terms.

evidence.what: CE closing receivables by customer, Dec-2024 vs Dec-2025, vs contractual terms
evidence.figures: Rheinkauf EUR 2,060,367 -> 4,493,177 (+2,432,809); implied DSO 55.6->116.2d vs 45d terms; Delta Benelux 50->73d, Nieuwmarkt 53->71d (40d terms); rest stable

evidence.what: CE receivables build vs flat collections through 2025
evidence.figures: CE closing AR EUR 4,734,545 (Jan) -> 8,470,059 (Dec); collections ~EUR 3.0-3.6m/month throughout; CE total AR up EUR 2.81m

recommended_action: Escalate Rheinkauf Gruppe as a credit/collections matter (dunning, credit-limit hold, provision review); the DSO cluster is one customer, not a CE-wide trend.

headline: April's +196% EBITDA spike is a one-off: EUR 2.2m other income booked to Nordics alongside a EUR 5.5m asset-disposal cash inflow; underlying April margin was the normal ~8.8%.

evidence.what: the only non-zero other income in the dataset
evidence.figures: EUR 2,200,000 other income, April-2025, all in Nordics; every other month across both years is zero
April investing cash flow EUR 5,500,000 (the only non-zero investing month); reported EBITDA 3,394,941 vs underlying 1,194,941 = 8.8% of net revenue, in line with the ~9% run-rate

recommended_action: Exclude the EUR 2.2m from run-rate and FY comparisons; note it lifts reported FY EBITDA and masks the Nordics underlying decline (F4).

headline: MISS: the pack never names the single driver behind the margin/EBITDA flags -- promotional discounting is up 3-5pp and cost the company ~EUR 3.9m of gross profit; the Baltics discount ladder is still climbing.
claimed_cause: Company gross margin fell 2.31pp (42.54% to 40.23%), roughly EUR 3.88m of gross profit foregone at 2025 volumes, driven by promo discount rate rising from 6.0% to 9.6% in Nordics (concentrated in Home Care, 6.0% to 18.8%) and 8.0% to 12.5% in Baltics with a monthly trajectory still rising to 17.1% by December. The flags surface this only as rising 'material cost' and rising 'net revenue', never as discount/price.

evidence.what: company gross margin and gross profit growth vs revenue growth
evidence.figures: GM 42.54%->40.23% (-2.31pp); gross profit +2.7% on net revenue +8.6%; EUR 3.88m gross profit foregone vs holding 2024 margin

evidence.what: discount rate by BU and the Baltics monthly ladder
evidence.figures: Nordics discount 6.0%->9.6% (Home Care 6.0%->18.8% on +41.9% volume); Baltics 8.0%->12.5%, rising each month 8.2% (Jan) to 17.1% (Dec); Central Europe held ~4.0%, margin +1.0pp

recommended_action: Give the board a gross-to-net (discount) bridge and set a discount-rate ceiling per BU/line; the Baltics upward trajectory means margin keeps eroding if left alone.

headline: MISS: the +8.6% revenue growth the monthly flags celebrate is entirely volume; price and mix destroyed EUR 8.9m, so the growth is margin-dilutive.
claimed_cause: The FY2025 price/volume/mix bridge shows net revenue up EUR 13.35m from volume +EUR 22.24m offset by mix -EUR 5.91m and price -EUR 2.98m. The monthly YoY net-revenue flags read as a string of positive beats, but the composition is falling realised prices and a shift to cheaper lines, which is why gross profit barely moved.

evidence.what: gross profit growth lagging revenue growth

recommended_action: Track net revenue split into volume/price/mix in the pack so the board sees growth quality, not just the top line.

headline: MISS: the EUR 15.8m rise in cash flatters the picture -- EUR 5.5m is a one-off disposal and operating cash conversion fell to 66%, with growth financed into receivables (+EUR 3.9m).
claimed_cause: 2025 operating cash flow was EUR 10.30m against underlying EBITDA of EUR 15.50m (66% conversion, down from 76% in 2024), because receivables grew EUR 3.86m over the year (Central Europe +EUR 2.81m, Baltics +EUR 1.16m, Nordics flat). Of the EUR 15.80m increase in closing cash, EUR 5.5m is the April asset disposal, not operations.

evidence.what: operating cash flow vs underlying EBITDA, 2024 vs 2025
evidence.figures: OCF 13.69m (2024) -> 10.30m (2025); OCF/underlying EBITDA 76.2% -> 66.4%; investing inflow 5.50m in 2025 (0 in 2024)

evidence.what: company receivables build over 2025 by BU
evidence.figures: AR opening 17.67m -> closing 21.53m (+3.86m); Central Europe +2.81m, Baltics +1.16m, Nordics -0.11m

recommended_action: Report operating cash conversion and separate one-off investing inflows from the cash headline; the AR build (F5) is the leak to fix.

headline: MISS: within Nordics, the high-value Skin & Body line is shrinking 13% while deeply discounted Home Care grows 42% -- a trade-down the BU-grain flags hide.
claimed_cause: Nordics volume mix moved toward its cheapest line: Home Care +41.9% (net EUR 2.18/unit, discount 18.8%) while Skin & Body -13.0% (net EUR 5.26/unit) and Hair Care/Professional roughly flat. The shift into low-value, deeply discounted volume is the mix driver behind the Nordics margin fall and is invisible in a BU-grain pack.

evidence.what: Nordics line-level volume, net price/unit and discount FY2024 vs FY2025
evidence.figures: Home Care volume +41.9%, net/unit 2.50->2.18 (-12.7%), discount 6.0%->18.8%; Skin & Body volume -13.0% at net/unit 5.26; other two lines +/-2.4%

recommended_action: Ask why Nordics Skin & Body volume is falling and whether the Home Care discount is defending share or destroying value; decide line by line.
